claims.text: Conventional strengthening approaches commonly improve strength at the cost of tensile ductility.
Applying SCCP to tungsten refractory high-entropy alloys enhances strength relative to processing without controlled coherent nanoprecipitation.
Applying SCCP to tungsten refractory high-entropy alloys enhances or maintains ductility relative to processing without controlled coherent nanoprecipitation.
Conventionally processed tungsten-based refractory alloys often exhibit brittle phases or limited ductility.
The SCCP process induces coherent nanoprecipitates in tungsten refractory high-entropy alloys.
The SCCP-induced coherent nanoprecipitates are uniformly distributed.
The nanoprecipitates have minimal lattice mismatch with the matrix.
Coherent nanoprecipitate interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission.
Coherent nanoprecipitate interfaces relieve or redistribute local stress concentrations.
Relieving local stress concentrations delays premature crack initiation.
The coherent interfaces delay crack propagation.
The combination of dislocation transmission and stress relief overcomes the strength-ductility trade-off.
An SCCP-designed tungsten refractory high-entropy alloy can exceed 2 GPa strength at ambient temperature.
An SCCP-designed tungsten refractory high-entropy alloy can achieve approximately 10-15% or greater tensile ductility at ambient temperature.
An SCCP-designed tungsten refractory high-entropy alloy will exceed 2 GPa strength at approximately 800 °C.
An SCCP-designed tungsten refractory high-entropy alloy will retain at least 10-15% tensile ductility at approximately 800 °C.
Brittle W-enriched BCC phases impede resolution of the strength-ductility trade-off in single-principal-element W alloy systems.
Traditional multi-principal-element processing methods typically produce brittle phases or limited ductility in tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloys.
The SCCP enhancement may not transfer directly to material systems lacking analogous coherent nanoprecipitation mechanisms.
The stability of the coherent interfaces at temperatures beyond the experimentally evaluated range remains unvalidated.
